# The Hackathon Playbook

> Battle-tested hackathon strategy from 36+ wins and $100K+ in prizes, by Bill Zhang.
> Covers team formation, ideation, validation, execution, pitching, submission, and
> what to do after the hackathon, plus a dedicated track for non-coders building with AI.

The playbook is a 7-phase system, ordered the way a hackathon actually unfolds; read
the phases in sequence for the full method, or jump to the phase you are in right now.
The non-coder track shows domain experts how to win with AI tools instead of code, and
ships installable AI skills (slash commands) for Cursor and Claude Code. The blog holds
long-form write-ups of specific strategies. Every page on this site has a Markdown
version at the same URL with .md appended, and llms-full.txt contains the whole corpus.
A read-only MCP server exposing search over this content lives at https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/api/mcp
(see https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json).

## Playbook

- [Team Formation](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/playbook/team-formation.md): Find the right people, define roles, and create a winning team dynamic.
- [Ideation](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/playbook/ideation.md): Brainstorm, evaluate, and select ideas that judges love and you can actually build.
- [Validation](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/playbook/validation.md): Validate your idea quickly against real constraints and judging criteria.
- [Execution](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/playbook/execution.md): Time management, tech stack selection, MVP strategy, and team coordination.
- [Pitching](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/playbook/pitching.md): Craft a pitch that wins judges over in the first 30 seconds.
- [Submission](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/playbook/submission.md): Write READMEs, record demos, and submit deliverables that make judges remember you.
- [Post-Hackathon](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/playbook/post-hackathon.md): Share your work, follow up with contacts, and turn weekend projects into career-changing portfolio pieces.

## For Non-Coders

- [The Proof](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/proof.md): Real professionals who beat thousands of developers at major hackathons.
- [Getting Started](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/setup.md): The 3 files, 4 shortcuts, and daily workflow you need to start building.
- [Concepts Explained](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/concepts.md): GitHub, APIs, deploying, and other jargon explained in plain English.
- [Using APIs](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/apis.md): How to add any service to your app with just a key and a docs link.
- [The System Prompt](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/system-prompt.md): The CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files that set the rules your AI follows every session. One command sets up both.
- [Skills & Commands](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills.md): Installable AI skills and slash commands that teach your AI to work with non-coders.

## AI Skills

- [Non-Coder Mode](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/non-coder-mode.md): Core guardrails for non-coders. Tells the AI to explain everything in plain English, break tasks into small steps, and never assume coding knowledge.
- [Domain to Spec](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/domain-to-spec.md): Run this FIRST. Captures your domain expertise and writes AGENTS.md and PRD.md to the repo root. Every other scaffold skill reads these files.
- [Quickstart](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/quickstart.md): One-shot project bootstrapper. Chains domain-to-spec, scaffold-frontend, and scaffold-backend (if needed) with user confirmation between steps.
- [Scaffold Frontend](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/scaffold-frontend.md): PRD-driven Next.js scaffold into clients/. Reads AGENTS.md and PRD.md, generates pages, layout, types, and an API client. Refuses to run without both files.
- [Scaffold Backend](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/scaffold-backend.md): PRD-driven FastAPI scaffold into server/ with optional Supabase. One stub route per entry in PRD.md > Backend Routes. Skips automatically if Backend Needed? = No.
- [v0 Prompt Crafter](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/v0-prompt-crafter.md): Turn a PRD or product description into a production-grade Vercel v0 prompt. Researches the industry, commits to a bold aesthetic, picks fancy UI libraries (shadcn, Aceternity, Magic UI, Motion), and assembles a copy-paste prompt.
- [Feature Builder](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/feature-builder.md): Structured workflow for implementing a new feature. Returns a plan, files list, commands, test steps, and rollback plan.
- [Bugfix Doctor](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/bugfix-doctor.md): Systematic bug-fixing workflow. Walks through reproduce, isolate, fix, test, and verify. Explains all errors in plain English.
- [Demo Prep](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/demo-prep.md): Produces a step-by-step live demo script for hackathon presentations. Covers the problem, walkthrough, and outcome with a backup plan.
- [GitHub Writer](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/non-coders/skills/readme-writer.md): Turns your finished project into a winner-grade GitHub README: a centered hero, badges, a clickable demo video, an architecture diagram, and team cards, then sets the repo's About description, website, and topics so recruiters and judges can find it.

## Blog

- [What to Do After a Hackathon: Ship 5 Assets That Get You Hired](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/blog/what-to-do-after-a-hackathon.md): What to do after a hackathon, win or lose: the 5 linked assets that get you hired, and the AI skills that build your README, Devpost, portfolio, and demo copy.
- [9 Hackathon Pitch Mistakes I Saw at LA Hacks](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/blog/hackathon-pitch-mistakes-la-hacks.md): Hackathon pitch mistakes from the LA Hacks judging floor: tailor the pitch, cut your slides, demo the main flow, and protect Q&A time for higher scores.
- [How to Win Hackathons: A Complete Guide from 36+ Victories](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/blog/how-to-win-hackathons.md): How to win hackathons, from 36+ wins and $100K+ in prizes. The 7-phase system covering team, ideation, validation, execution, pitching, and submission.
- [Best Tech Stack for Hackathons in 2026: Tools That Win Prizes](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/blog/best-tech-stack-for-hackathons.md): The best tech stack for hackathons in 2026: Next.js, FastAPI, Supabase, Vercel, and an AI API. The exact stack winning teams use, and the rule that beats it.
- [Hackathon Tips for Beginners: Your First Hackathon Survival Guide](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/blog/hackathon-tips-for-beginners.md): First hackathon? This beginner's guide covers what to bring, how to find a team, what to build, the mistakes to avoid, and how to win as a first-timer.
- [Hackathon Pitch Guide: How to Present Your Project and Win Prizes](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/blog/hackathon-pitch-guide.md): Master the hackathon pitch with a 3-minute structure from 36+ winning presentations: the hook, the demo, judge Q&A, and the mistakes that cost prizes.
- [Non-Coders Winning Hackathons: How Experts Beat Developers](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/blog/non-coders-winning-hackathons.md): Non-coders winning hackathons is real in 2026. A lawyer took 1st and a doctor 3rd at Anthropic SF, beating developers with AI tools like Cursor and Claude Code.
- [How to Build with ElevenLabs and Cursor at a Hackathon](https://thehackathonplaybook.dev/blog/build-with-elevenlabs-and-cursor.md): Build a voice AI hackathon project with ElevenLabs and Cursor in an afternoon. The exact PRD-first, MCP-driven, test-driven workflow Bill uses to ship and win.
